one_month_reasoning: No Micron earnings in the window (FQ1 FY27 report expected mid/late Dec 2026). Events by 30 Oct (last session before 1 Nov): Samsung Q3 preliminary guidance (early/mid Oct) and full Q3 results with SK hynix Q3 results (late Oct). Kioxia Q2 FY26 results on 30 Oct [17]. Hyperscaler capex prints and the FOMC fall in the last week of Oct. Memory-price trackers update monthly. Peers are reporting into the same supply-constrained market Micron described [3], so beats are likely but already priced in. Post-earnings drift: FQ1 guide was ~8% above consensus [1][18], but the stock gained only +0.9% vs the pre-print close and faded on 2 Oct, so drift support is weak. Because MU beat its own guide by less each quarter (EPS +45% in FQ2, +31% in FQ3, +8% in FQ4 [11][12][13][1]), I see no strong directional edge. I use a near-symmetric lognormal centred at ~$1,085 (+1% drift) with ~21% monthly sigma, a bit below 80%/3.5 because part of the realized vol came from the trend.

fair_value.method: Blend: 50% P/E (FY28 EPS $195 x 5.5x = $1,073), 30% EV/EBITDA (FY28 EBITDA $254B x 4.0x + ~$202B adj. net cash = $1,059) and 20% through-cycle DCF ($777, assumes the cycle rolls over after FY28). Blended about $1,010 per share for Oct 2027.

inputs_detail.derivation: FY28 consensus $205.95 [18] cut ~5%. Mgmt guides a 'more moderate rate of price increases' and opex +$2.5B [3]. Bit growth is only ~low-20s% [3].
FQ1 guide $38.15 [1], with sequential growth every quarter and GM rising after FQ1 [3] (~$44/$48.5/$52). That gives ~$183, blended with consensus $176.42 [18].

Inside the peer range of 3.97-23.73x and the memory-maker range of 3.97-8.04x. Slightly above the 4.7x peer median because MU trades at 6.1x today. Applied one year later, when the market looks through to FY29, the cycle is further along, so there is no expansion.
FQ1 guidance share count. Buybacks resume after 9 Dec 2026 [7] and could trim the count; this is ignored for conservatism.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: FY28 EBITDA $254B x 4.0x = EV $1,016B, plus adj. net cash $202B, divided by 1.15B shares

inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus $314.16B [18] cut ~5% for moderating price increases [3].
FQ4 was 82.3% [3] and FQ1 GM guide is 86.25% with opex rising [1][3]. Trimmed for higher opex and possible price plateau.
FY26 D&A $9.5B [1], with FY27 capex likely >$50B (1H ~$25B, 2H higher) [3].
Equals the 10-peer derived forward EV/EBITDA median (~4.0x). The memory-maker subset median is ~3.2x.

Starts from $68.3B net cash [3]. Adds FY27 FCF ~$154B (OCF ~$209B less capex ~$55B) [1][3]. Subtracts dividends and ~$20B of SCA customer deposits, which are refundable later [3] and treated as debt-like (now $12.9B [1]).

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: WACC 11%. FCF FY28 $160B, FY29 $110B, FY30 $60B, FY31 $50B. Terminal FCF $45B growing 3%. Plus $202B net cash, divided by 1.15B shares, valued at Oct 2027.

inputs_detail.derivation: Cyclical roll-off after the cleanroom wave of late 2028 onward [3]. The 10-K warns supply additions can drive ASP declines [8]. RPO ~$150B at floor prices [3] (vs ~$5B in May [6]) supports a non-trivial floor.
High-beta cyclical with top-10 customer concentration ~50% of revenue [8]. Equity-funded with net cash.
Roughly 2/3 of FY26 adjusted FCF of $62.3B [1], reflecting a structurally larger, more contracted business [3] but mid-cycle pricing.

bear.story: By mid-2027 the market starts pricing the 2028-29 cleanroom wave (Micron ID1/ID2, Japan, Singapore [3], plus peers' capex). Spot/contract price momentum stalls and the stock de-rates to ~3x peak EPS, as in past memory peaks when shares halved while earnings were still rising. Floor-priced SCAs/RPO [3] limit the EPS damage but not the multiple.

base.story: FY27 delivers ~$180 EPS with sequential growth [3]. Buybacks restart after the CHIPS restriction lapses on 9 Dec 2026 [7]. Supply stays tight through 2028 per management, but investors keep a 5-6x NTM multiple on what they view as peak earnings.

bull.story: Tightness extends visibly into 2029. HBM pricing resets higher in CY27 [5]. SCAs (35%+ of revenue, floors above prior-cycle peak margins [3]) convince investors that earnings are less cyclical, and MU re-rates to ~8x FY28-29 EPS of $210-230, the top of the memory peer range (Sandisk 8x).

comps_summary.peer_range: Fwd P/E 3.97-23.73x across 10 peers, 3.97-8.04x for the 8 memory/NAND names. Derived fwd EV/EBITDA 2.3-6.7x for memory names; HDD makers are much higher (16.9x STX, ~30x WDC trailing). Fwd EV/EBITDA derived: trailing EV/EBITDA x (fwd P/E / trailing P/E).
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 5.5x NTM P/E and 4.0x EV/EBITDA. Both are inside the peer range: P/E sits slightly above the 4.7x median and below MU's current 6.1x on FY27; EV/EBITDA is at the median.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: I claim no structural premium. The slight P/E position above the median reflects MU's current trading level and is within the range. A durable premium would need evidence that SCA floors ($150B RPO at minimum prices [3]) and $68B net cash [3] reduce earnings cyclicality through the horizon. That is plausible but unproven before a downturn tests the floors, so it appears only in the bull case. HDD names (WDC, STX) trade far higher on a different supply structure and were not used to lift the multiple.

thesis_break_reason: $640 is ~40% below spot and ~3.1x FY28 consensus EPS [18]. Trading there would most likely mean the market sees a memory price peak: contract prices flattening or falling, SCA renegotiation or deposit pull-back, or hyperscaler capex cuts. That contradicts management's 'much tighter in 2027 and 2028' and 'no line of sight to balance' [3], which is the core of my thesis. Ordinary 80%-vol noise alone is less likely to take it there inside a year without a fundamental trigger.

key_uncertainties: Timing of the memory price peak relative to the 2028 cleanroom wave (Micron, Samsung, SK hynix, Kioxia capex all rising).
Whether SCA floors and take-or-pay volumes hold in a downturn; deposits are refundable later in each term [3].
Multiple regime: the market has historically paid ~3-6x peak memory EPS; a re-rating either way dominates EPS changes.
Size and pace of buybacks after 9 Dec 2026 [7]; no amount was given [4].
Decaying beat magnitude vs own guidance (EPS +45% in FQ2, +31% in FQ3, +8% in FQ4) [11][12][13][1].
Litigation tail (Netlist $445M verdict on appeal, YMTC suits) [6]: small relative to earnings.
reasoning: Primary documents show an exceptionally strong position. FQ4 revenue was $54.2B (14 weeks) at 87% GM and $33.42 EPS [1]. The FQ1 guide is $61.5B/$38.15 [1], ~8% above consensus [18]. Management calls FQ1 the FY27 GM floor with sequential growth every quarter [3]. SCAs are signed and RPO is ~$150B at floor prices [3], up from ~$5B in the May 10-Q [6]. Customer deposits are $12.7B, and >75% of FY27 output is committed [5]. Net cash is $68.3B [3]. Note that most of the CHIPS buyback restriction lapses 9 Dec 2026 [7]. Against this: MU already trades at ~6.1x FY27 and ~5.2x FY28 consensus EPS [18], right where memory peers sit (median ~4.7x [19-28]). The market prices these earnings as cyclical-peak. The 10-K flags that supply additions drive ASP declines [8], and management is raising capex sharply for cleanrooms available from late CY28 [3], as peers expand too. My fair value of ~$1,010 is a 50/30/20 blend of P/E (5.5x FY28 $195), EV/EBITDA (4.0x) and a through-cycle DCF. That is close to spot, so 12-month return depends mainly on whether the cycle's end is pushed out (bull) or starts to be priced (bear). Scenarios: $560/25%, $1,100/50%, $1,800/25% (mean ~$1,140). I built the ladder from a mixture of lognormals around these (sigma 22-32%), implying ~65-70% effective annual vol vs 80% realized, plus fat tails. The median is ~$1,080, P(>=spot) ~0.52, and P(halving) ~10%. Research was limited: Twelve Data statistics/targets and Alpha Vantage were plan/rate-limited, so peer multiples come from StockAnalysis pages, and forward EV/EBITDA and peer growth are derived approximations.
